clue.text: Left going in terribly straight to produce shiner

indicators.note: going in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
terribly suggests the letters of straight are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone straightens up awkwardly, as if to show off a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles STRAIGHT and 'going in' puts L (Left) inside it. A 'shiner' looks like slang for a black eye, but here it is just something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the stars shines down on us, so starlight is literally a shiner.

definitions.meaning: a wise teacher, like a guru

explanation.surface: A short list pairing a kitchen plant with a spiritual teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an aromatic culinary plant and a wise, venerated person.

definitions.note: the word 'the' is an example of the part of speech this answer names

indicators.note: a pitiful performance is a wretched mess, so the letters of recital are jumbled

explanation.surface: A critic sums up a dreadful concert: the recital is pitiful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link joining the definition to the wordplay. The definition reads 'the' as an instance, since 'the' is the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so it is an example of this word class.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words, spanning their junction

explanation.surface: An omen appears in a time of looming trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Lanky, like a group of criminals might you say?

parts.note: a gang is a band of criminals
the suffix -ly turns a noun into an adjective meaning in the manner of that thing

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a gawky figure looks like a criminal mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful 'might you say?' admits the joke: GANG with -LY added would mean 'in the manner of a gang'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangly describes someone tall, thin and awkward in build, which is what lanky means.

clue.text: Leader, first of those on hand?

definitions.meaning: the boss or most important person
a bunch of bananas is called a hand, so the top one is literally the first banana there

explanation.surface: Asking who is in charge among the people present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' looks like 'available', but a cluster of bananas on the stem is a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal for the chief or most important person in a group.

definitions.meaning: the joint between thigh and pelvis

explanation.surface: Describing a trendy nightspot, or a cannabis cigarette in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for trendy and also the ball-and-socket joint of the pelvis.

definitions.meaning: the ... of something is its centre
a ... is a playing card of the ... suit

explanation.surface: Pointing to the card in the centre of a spread hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means the core or centre, and it is also a playing card from one of the four suits.

clue.text: Little time invested in ropey novel, creative work

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
novel means new, so the letters of ropey take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: T is the short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An author spent barely any time on a poor novel and calls it creative work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal: OPREY (ROPEY rearranged) takes T inside, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is an imaginative literary art, so poems are a kind of creative work.

definitions.meaning: to ... from a vehicle is to alight
...! is an exhortation to dance energetically

explanation.surface: A disco caller tells passengers to step off and dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both stepping down from a bus or horse and dancing with abandon.

indicators.note: over a phone line we only hear the word, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a plaice is a flatfish, a swimmer in crossword terms

explanation.surface: An odd request to hand a swimming champion the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' means a fish here; PLAICE, a British flatfish, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to put it in position, so the two verbs are synonyms.

indicators.note: organise means arrange afresh, so the letters of the classroom are put into new order

explanation.surface: Wondering who would keep a classroom in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'organise' rearranges THE CLASSROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A male teacher in a school runs the classroom, so he is the one who organises it.

clue.text: Under pressure to answer, perhaps, immediately

definitions.meaning: being put ... means being forced to respond at once

explanation.surface: Someone squirming when asked to reply right now.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both being pressed for a response and acting instantly, without delay.

definitions.meaning: the past tense of feel, to touch with the fingers

explanation.surface: A shopper running a hand across fabric in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of touching and also a matted textile.

clue.text: As lute starts, organ starts too

indicators.note: starts means we take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A concert where the organ joins in as the lute begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of As, lute, starts and organ spell the answer; the first 'starts' is itself one of the words picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Darling goes after bargain a bit

indicators.note: goes after places the first piece named after the second in the answer

parts.note: a snip is a bargain in British slang
pet is a term of endearment like darling

explanation.surface: A beloved partner chasing a shopping deal.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIP is British for a bargain ('a snip at the price').
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Sweet animal picked up by the ears?

indicators.note: what the ears pick up is a sound, so the answer is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A cute creature lifted by its ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up by the ears' looks like lifting a rabbit, but it signals hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dessert, a sweet in British usage.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A traveller names Seoul as a capital they visited in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Seoul is a red herring capital; the answer runs across 'Asia then, Seoul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Somewhere for the players to hear script that's rewritten

indicators.note: a script that is rewritten has its contents reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors gathering to listen to a revised script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like actors, but they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the sunken area in front of a stage where musicians play.

clue.text: On top of elevated location, caught cold

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece named second sits above the first

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hill is a raised piece of ground

explanation.surface: A walker caught a cold up on a high spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild cold or feverish shivering, and also means coldness.

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me
sh is a call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone telling their own social network to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a net-like fabric of interlaced threads, a network of strands.

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means the first piece named comes after the second

parts.note: to brush is to touch lightly, to skim

explanation.surface: Advice not to waste money on a paintbrush.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy, to economise rather than spend freely.

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Describing an old flame as a big specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a sample or specimen that typifies its kind.

clue.text: This person is underlining a point

indicators.note: in a down answer, underlining puts the first piece beneath the second

parts.note: the speaker saying 'I am' gives the contraction I'm

explanation.surface: A speaker stressing that they are underlining a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person is' contracts to I'M, written under A.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim a weapon is to point it at a target.

indicators.note: no head means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: peel is the skin of fruit

explanation.surface: A cook prepares fish, keeping the skin but discarding the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snake-like fish.

parts.note: a test is a trial or try
to match is to fit or suit

explanation.surface: An athlete trying to get fit for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket or rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby, so it is a game.
